FUTURE PARTY / 2050← 2050 Research

Projection 2050 · the wall film, recut

Further

The first cut, Already Here, showed the present dressed as the future: a 1982 river gate, a 2004 train, two lab printers and a lettuce. The recut is 16 bold claims for 2030 to 2050. Each one sits on a real seed that has already happened and on the most beautiful free image of it, from observatories, NASA artists and night photography.

  • 15v1 slides cut
  • 6demoted to burst frames
  • 16new claims, each with a dated seed
  • 37images, all PD, CC0 or CC
  • 74.6 sseamless 1080p loop, silent

The full 1080p films are on the v3.0 release.

The roast

One frame per v1 slide, taken from the render, so this is what guests actually saw. Verdicts: cut, kept only as a one-third-second burst frame, or kept and promoted.

  1. 01 Supertrees, Singapore, "Towers that grow gardens"

    Steel sculptures with creepers, shot at noon under a grey sky. At night they glow like Pandora, and we used the daylight one.

    Replace

  2. 02 Lujiazui, "The city of tomorrow"

    Best photo in the chapter, worst caption in the reel: it is what a stock site titles a skyline.

    Burst only

  3. 03 Noor solar, "Solar fields to the horizon"

    Half the frame is beige dirt and the horizon is haze. On a wall it is a beige rectangle.

    Cut

  4. 04 Shanghai Maglev, "Trains that float"

    The caption admits it has run since 2004. A train parked beside a car park.

    Cut

  5. 05 Waymo, "Cars that drive themselves"

    A white SUV with a bucket on its head, cranes behind. Dashcam energy.

    Cut

  6. 06 Thames Barrier, "A wall against the sea"

    Blade Runner 2049's wall is a coastline of black concrete. This is a 1982 river gate in fog, grey on grey.

    Cut

  7. 07 Eden Project, "Gardens under domes"

    Bubble wrap in Cornwall, opened 2001, under an overcast sky. The Wild Robot link is invented.

    Cut

  8. 08 Block Island wind, "Power from the open sea"

    Five turbines the size of matchsticks. 90% of the frame is empty water.

    Cut

  9. 09 Sophia, "A machine with a face"

    A 2016 PR puppet with a see-through skull. Uncanny, not inspiring.

    Cut

  10. 10 Robonaut 2, "Robots working beside us"

    The robot came home broken in 2018. Headless-looking in a cluttered module.

    Cut

  11. 11 Apple Vision Pro, "Screens you move by hand"

    A product on a shop table with shoppers' legs behind it. Minority Report had no headset.

    Cut

  12. 12 Frontier, "A mind made of machines"

    Server racks and yellow cable trays: the least cinematic object in tech, with a logo.

    Cut

  13. 13 BGI sequencers, "Reading the genome"

    Two beige printers in a white room. The ugliest frame in the reel.

    Cut

  14. 14 Vertical farm, "Farms without fields"

    Nice symmetry, but it is shelving with lettuce, and the claim is tame.

    Cut

  15. 15 Ingenuity, "A robot alone in the wild"

    The helicopter is about 40 px tall on a beige plain. Great story, invisible image.

    Cut

  16. 16 Artemis I launch, "Leaving Earth again"

    Strong moment, but the rocket is a small bright stick in a mostly black frame.

    Burst only

  17. 17 Crew Dragon and the ISS, "Docking with a station"

    Clean and real, but 2001 showed it in 1968. A "now", not a "next".

    Burst only

  18. 18 Veggie lettuce, "Food grown in space"

    A hot-pink close-up of salad as the space chapter's climax.

    Cut

  19. 19 Perseverance, "Working on Mars"

    Strong, real, well lit.

    Burst only

  20. 20 Stanford torus, 1975, "A ring-shaped home in orbit"

    The most beautiful frame in the reel and its only radical idea, and we apologised for it with a "Then" label. This is the tell: the future people want is the part not built yet.

    Keep, promote

  21. 21 Saturn, "Saturn's rings up close"

    Textbook-diagram lighting in a black box. Cassini's backlit "Day the Earth Smiled" is ten times the image.

    Replace

  22. 22 M87*, "Seeing a black hole"

    A scientific triumph and a visual smudge: a blurry orange ring on 80% black.

    Cut

  23. 23 Cosmic Cliffs, "A window on deep space"

    The best image in the reel.

    Burst

  24. 24 Orion, "A ship between Earth and Moon"

    Earth and Moon in one frame, strong.

    Burst only

  25. 25 Earthrise, "We saw home"

    Iconic, but Earth is small on a black field, and a projector shows black as bare wall.

    Replace the closer

The recut

Each slide states a target year, a film that genuinely imagined it, the claim, then the seed: a dated fact that makes the claim less crazy than it sounds. Frames are from the final render.

How far to trust it

  • The years are editorial forecasts built on stated targets, not promises. Colossal's 2028 calf would be a gene-edited Asian elephant, not a true mammoth. CFS's early-2030s plant needs SPARC to work and a grid review that can take four to six years.
  • Obayashi's own engineer said 2050 is "not our goal or promise". CERN's final FCC decision is due around 2028. The ELT's first light is planned for March 2029.
  • HAVOC was a NASA Langley concept study, never a funded mission. Starshot is a research programme with no launch date.
  • The space-elevator image is a screenshot from the game Ace Combat 7 (Bandai Namco, CC BY 3.0). It is credited on screen as a game image.
  • The Venus slide is darkened so the orange line passes contrast on a washed-out projector, which costs some of the bright cloud deck.
  • There are no AI-generated images and no sound. Both are deliberate, and both can be added.
